To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we solved the structure of the AAV/AAVR complex to 2.4 A resolution and that this structure explains why AAVR is an AAV-specific receptor, and how it interacts with the AAV capsid.
the structure of the gene therapy virus, adeno-associated-virus (AAV), bound to its receptor, AAV receptor (AAVR), has been solved at 2.3 Å resolution.
the structure and function of the AAVR-AAV complex has been determined by combining cryo-EM with cryo-ET, and the structure provides a roadmap to manipulate the complex.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the molecular basis of gene therapy.
the molecular mechanisms underlying the specificity of AAV vectors.
the molecular basis for AAV’s tropism, and the implications for the development of gene therapy vectors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the structure of AAVR and the AAVR- AAV complex provides the foundation for a new understanding of AAV cell tropism and a new approach to engineering tissue-specific AAV vectors.
the structure of the adeno-associated virus ( AAV) with its cell receptor (AAVR) provides a roadmap for the engineering of tissue-specific vectors.
this study has provided a high resolution structure of a virus-receptor complex, which is a key to understanding the cell entry and trafficking of the AAV vector.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the structure provides a roadmap to experimentally probe and manipulate viral-receptor interactions, which is key to understanding cell entry and trafficking, and will be needed to engineer tissue specific vectors.
the AAVR structure is a critical component in the design and engineering of next generation of AAV-based gene therapy vectors.
we have solved the structure of a virus interacting with its cell receptor at near-atomic resolution.
The main takeaway from our work is that
AAV’s receptor, AAV receptor (AAVR), binds in between the viral spikes, on top of a conserved plateau.
the structure of the AAV/AAVR complex is consistent with a model in which AAVR binds to the viral capsid between the pentameric spikes and the icosahedral capsid lattice.
AAVR binds to AAV between the spikes in a region that is conserved except in one clonal lineage.
